title: Baechu Geotjeori Fresh Kimchi
shortDescription: Bite-size napa cabbage is briefly salted and tossed with a fresh gochugaru, fish-sauce, garlic, scallion, and sesame dressing for same-day serving.
culturalContext: Geotjeori describes freshly seasoned vegetables intended to be eaten before long fermentation. Baechu geotjeori brings crisp cabbage and an immediate, lively seasoning to the table; household formulas and sweetness vary.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.item: Korean plum syrup or rice syrup

instructions.heading: Cut and wash the cabbage
instructions.action: Remove damaged outer leaves, cut cabbage into bite-size pieces, and wash under cool running water. Drain briefly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Pieces include both leafy and crisp stem portions and no grit remains.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean board and potable running water.

instructions.heading: Salt
instructions.action: Toss cabbage with salt in a nonreactive bowl. Rest 40 minutes, turning every 10 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Stem pieces bend slightly but retain a juicy crunch.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep covered and separate from raw animal foods.

instructions.heading: Rinse and drain
instructions.action: Rinse thoroughly under cold running water and drain 10 minutes, shaking off trapped water.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: No salt crystals remain and the cabbage is moist but not dripping.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a sanitized colander and sink area.

instructions.heading: Mix the dressing
instructions.action: In the cleaned bowl, combine gochugaru, fish sauce, plum syrup, garlic, scallions, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The dressing is loose, vivid red, and evenly mixed.
instructions.safetyNote: Contains fish and sesame; verify packaged ingredient labels.

instructions.heading: Toss
instructions.action: Wearing gloves, gently toss drained cabbage with dressing until every piece is lightly coated.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cabbage looks glossy and red while the leaves remain distinct rather than crushed.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean food-safe gloves and a clean serving dish.

instructions.heading: Serve or chill
instructions.action: Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate for up to 1 hour before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The stems remain crisp and little liquid has accumulated.
instructions.safetyNote: Refrigerate promptly; geotjeori is a fresh banchan, not a room-temperature fermentation project.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan does not use a grill.
visualDonenessCues: Salted cabbage bends slightly but stays crisp
Finished geotjeori remains fresh and glossy
foodSafetyNotes: Wash cabbage under cool running water before preparation.
Use clean tools, gloves, and serving ware.
Refrigerate promptly at or below 40°F / 4°C; do not hold at room temperature to ferment.
Discard if mold, putrid odor, or unusual discoloration develops.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains fish and sesame; check syrup, gochugaru, and fish-sauce labels for facility cross-contact.

substitutions: Rice syrup may replace Korean plum syrup, with sweetness adjusted only after testing.
A vegan version needs a separately tested seasoning formula.
ingredientSourcing: Choose crisp napa cabbage without browned or slimy leaves.
Korean markets stock gochugaru, fish sauce, plum syrup, and toasted sesame oil.
makeAhead: Wash and cut cabbage several hours ahead and refrigerate dry; salt and dress close to serving.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container and use within 3 days; texture is best on day 1 and the limit requires food-safety review.
reheating: Do not reheat; serve cold or cool.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftover geotjeori as a cold rice topping within the approved storage window.
servingSuggestions: Pair with grilled meats or a warm soup

faq.question: Is geotjeori fermented kimchi?
faq.answer: It is designed to be eaten freshly seasoned; it may change slightly in the refrigerator but this recipe does not call for room-temperature fermentation.

faq.question: Why drain the cabbage well?
faq.answer: Excess water dilutes the seasoning and makes the fresh banchan watery sooner.
